criteria.label: Idea and Innovation
criteria.description: How creative and useful the idea is for a real-world problem.

criteria.label: Technicality
criteria.description: How well the project blends different technologies.

criteria.label: Design
criteria.description: Quality of design, including user experience and accessibility.

criteria.label: Pitching Clarity
criteria.description: A well-organized pitch with a clean, effective demo.

criteria.label: Time
criteria.description: Keeping to the limit: 5 minutes for general judging, 3 for sponsor judging.

criteria.label: Completion
criteria.description: How complete the hack is relative to the team's goals.

criteria.label: Theme
criteria.description: Relevance to the event theme, and the team's justification.

judging.judge_profile_summary: About 70 listed judges: in-person general judges without stated affiliation plus sponsor judges from Google, 1Password, Backboard.io, Foresters Financial, TwelveLabs, Amplitude, Shopify and Sentra.
judging.notes: Two of seven criteria are about the pitch itself (clarity and time). Five minutes for general judging, three for sponsor judging.

submission_requirements: Devpost submission with a demo video and a public GitHub repository
Relate the project to the event theme

sources.note: Dates, venue, participants, prizes, judges, judging criteria, pitch time limits.
Team size: up to four registered participants.
All 7 pages captured: 160 of 160 submissions; prize names from each of the 21 winning project pages.

curator_notes: The Devpost page asks teams to relate projects to a theme without naming it; many submissions frame themselves around identity, which suggests the theme (curator inference, unconfirmed). Taglines are CrafterWIKI paraphrases; domains assigned conservatively. The top three overall are analyzed records.
